Instead, whenever it's possible, prefer to move data, or when it's not possible, use smart pointers such as Rc and Arc for long-lived references,' presented as a goal the whole book was written to prove.

Contradicts own-lifetime-elision, which documents when explicit lifetimes ARE required (structs holding references, multiple ambiguous inputs); contradicts own-arc-shared, which scopes Arc to shared ownership crossing thread boundaries rather than as a general substitute for borrows; and contradicts own-borrow-over-clone. The chapter's parallel advice on macros ('think twice before writing a macro') is instead ALIGNED with macro-prefer-functions, so this is not a wholesale deviation chapter. It also does not establish whether the book's earlier chapters actually follow the no-lifetimes rule in their code.
